prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help pick the best Airbnb for your family — but to give specific listings I need a few details. Meanwhile, here’s quick guidance so you get the right place.

Quick questions
- What are your dates (or date range)?
- Budget per night (or total)?
- Do you need 2 bedrooms or 3? (Are kids sharing a bed or need separate beds?)
- Any must-haves: parking, crib/high chair, fenced yard, washer/dryer, elevator, ground-floor, pet-friendly, close to downtown, stroller accessibility?
- Do you want walkable restaurants/parks nearby or a quieter residential stay?

Where to look (neighborhoods and why)
- 12South — very walkable, family-friendly restaurants and parks; cute houses/duplexes. Great if you want neighborhood charm.
- Germantown — quieter, close to downtown and attractions (Ryman, riverfront), good restaurants and new condos.
- East Nashville — artsy, relaxed, many family homes with yards; good value.
- Sylvan Park / Hillsboro Village — very residential, good for families, close to greenways and small shops.
- The Gulch / Downtown — very central if you want to be within walking distance of music venues and tourist sites, but can be pricier and noisier.
- Green Hills — upscale, more suburban, near shopping (may be further from downtown).

Type of rental that works best for a family of 4
- Entire home or apartment with 2+ bedrooms and 1.5+ baths
- Full kitchen, washer/dryer, free parking (or dedicated on-site spot)
- Yard or nearby park for kids to play
- Self check-in and responsive host
- Child gear available (crib, high chair) if needed

Budget (rough)
- Expect midrange 2BR: $150–$300/night depending on neighborhood and season
- Downtown/Gulch and popular weekends: $250–$450+
- Suburban/less-central areas often cheaper

How to filter and what to check on Airbnb
- Filter: “Entire place,” 2+ bedrooms, family/kid friendly, crib if needed
- Amenities: washer, kitchen, free parking, self-check-in, air conditioning
- Read recent reviews for noise, cleanliness, and host responsiveness
- Check sleeping arrangements and exact bed types
- Confirm stairs/elevator if you have a stroller or mobility needs
- Check cancellation policy and total price (cleaning fee + taxes)

Safety and rules
- Nashville has neighborhood rules and short-term rental taxes — confirm the listing is legal and has good reviews
- If you need quiet nights for kids, avoid Broadway-adjacent listings (loud at night)

If you want, tell me your dates, budget, and must-haves and I’ll find 3–5 specific listings or recommend the single best option for your family.
